issues.detail: The Greek 'ουχ αρπαγμον ηγησατο το ειναι ισα θεω' means 'he did not consider himself to be equal to God' (or 'did not consider being equal to God as a robbery'). The Vietnamese translation 'chẳng coi sự mình bằng Đức Chúa Trời là sự cướp' translates 'αρπαγμον' as 'cướp' (robbery/theft), which is a literal but potentially misleading rendering of the Greek nuance. More importantly, the Greek structure implies he did not consider *himself* to be equal; the Vietnamese 'sự mình bằng Đức Chúa Trời' (one's being equal to God) loses the specific reflexive sense of 'ηγησατο' (considered/thought) regarding his own status.
